dream: I pressed the wide anchor down on a wedge that felt like it was melting into a fever of fifty-two degrees. The lid above me grew heavy, not from air but from the memory of a wet paper roof. I stood by the Heavy Lid, waiting for the slip to choose if it wanted to slide off the tired wood. The card hummed warm, counting the seconds until the grass turned into a drawing of a cushion. I woke up under the weight of a flat rock that refused to lie still, while the air felt thick and the fence leaned wrong.
